A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with LIT renamed L2T. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original multimodal benchmark comparisons, hallucination evaluations, ablations, and computational measurements in Section 3 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds original Prism-7B comparisons, text-only evaluations, attention visualizations, and a self-training pilot.

M1.justification: The joint instruction-response loss and template removal remain unchanged; LIT becomes L2T. However, Section 3.4 adds a pilot extension that generates instruction-response pairs from image-only inputs, combines them with original data, and continues fine-tuning.

E1.justification: v2 substantially broadens evaluation coverage with MT-Bench, WildBench, MMLU, and AGIEval text-only tasks. Its Prism evaluation adds RefCOCO+/RefCOCOg and VSR, evaluates RefCOCO as localization rather than the earlier captioning task, and reports AI2D evaluation results where v1 only listed AI2D among training sources.

E2.justification: v2 Table 6 adds an evaluated VIT-style Prism-7B comparator, specifically Prism-DINOSigLIP-Controlled-7B, against its L2T counterpart. The original TinyLLaVA, LLaVA-1.5, and LLaVA-NeXT comparison sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Existing training hyperparameters and evaluation settings are retained. New experiments introduce the Prism configuration, matched LLaVA-1.5 text-only comparisons, and a separate design starting from 100k training examples and adding 100k generated pairs for continued fine-tuning. Appendix F also introduces an attention-analysis protocol using 14 final-layer heads.

E4.justification: v2 adds attention analyses testing visual-token reliance, text-only tests examining possible language degradation, and a pilot testing benefits from self-generated supervision. These extend the substantive analysis beyond v1's retained loss, data-scale, data-type, template-removal, and computational studies.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-seed benchmark statistics, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The throughput mean-plus/minus reporting and averaging over 100 training steps are unchanged; the new benchmark tables also report point estimates.

E6.justification: All matched original numerical tables are unchanged, but v2 Tables 5-7 add substantial results. New VIT/L2T Prism comparisons include VSR scores of 53.20 versus 61.70. Text-only results show two gains and two small declines. The self-training pilot improves seven of eight scores, including RefCOCO-L from 17.42 to 24.53, while Flickr30k-L decreases from 68.55 to 68.32. These are new comparisons, not revised v1 scores.

T1.justification: The VIT and joint instruction-response objectives, visual-contribution definition, and CHAIR formulas are unchanged. v2 introduces no new formal assumptions, propositions, proofs, or mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central claims about instruction learning as regularization, improved visual capabilities and hallucination mitigation, and negligible computational overhead. Renaming LIT to L2T and adding supporting experiments do not alter these main claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning language-ability preservation and self-improvement through generated supervision. New Appendix G substantially extends the applicability argument by claiming that improved SFT grounding supports safer subsequent RL/RLHF alignment, although no alignment experiment tests this claim. The original limitations remain unchanged, moving from Appendix F to H.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link in the abstract and technical information for the new experiments. Appendix F specifies the selected pre-answer token, transformer layer and heads, sample sources, and example prompts. Existing hyperparameters, hardware disclosures, template lists, and CHAIR implementation details are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Prismatic VLMs, Orgad and Shen's work motivating attention analysis, and several 2025 multimodal studies. Appendix G adds positioning relative to RL/RLHF. The established novelty comparison with instruction modeling and the main related-work discussion remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose is retained with limited editing and the LIT-to-L2T rename. v2 adds experimental and appendix subsections, updates author information, adds acknowledgements, and moves the Impact Statement to Appendix I as Broader Impact. The original narrative and section sequence remain recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the two-column main-text layout with a predominantly single-column layout using wrapped displays, extensively resizing and relocating existing material. It adds attention Figures 6 and 12 and Tables 5-7 and 12. Existing ablation tables and qualitative examples are retained under new numbering.

improvement.justification: The Prism and text-only comparisons fill useful gaps in v1's evidence about model transfer and language retention; attention visualizations and the code link also improve assessability. These are incremental gains over an already extensive evaluation. Sparse details for new experiments, the self-training pilot's additional data and training, and untested RL/RLHF claims limit the strength of the added conclusions.
